quotes.text: But if the rows themselves are making round trips over the network, no amount of clever code will win. You're simply locked into bandwidth drag.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why data movement, not code, is the real bottleneck.

quotes.text: batch size is a knob that lets you choose between throughput and resource safety, and only trial runs tell you where your system maxes out.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames batch size tuning as a measurable trade-off rather than a default.

quotes.text: Beyond speed, this has a stability payoff. Predefining factor levels ensures that training and scoring data agree on how categories are encoded.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows that factor definitions matter for model stability, not only speed.

quotes.text: That's why the rule is simple. Transform before the model loop, never during it. Treat this as table stakes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable rule for staging transformations in SQL instead of R.

quotes.text: Here's the bottom line. Performance gains don't come from flashy algorithms. They come from discipline. In setup, there are three rules worth burning into memory.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the episode's thesis about disciplined setup.

chapters.title: Three rules for fast R-SQL pipelines

takeaways: Use the SQL Server compute context for large data so R runs next to the data instead of pulling every row across the network.
Tune the batch size step by step while watching memory, and write lean, well-shaped queries so the optimizer can build parallel plans.
Do transformations in T-SQL views or staging tables before the model loop, and define factor levels up front with colInfo for speed and stable models.
hook: Slow R pipelines on SQL Server are usually caused by setup, not algorithms. This episode helps data scientists and SQL professionals fix compute context, batch size, query shape, transformations and factor handling so R-SQL workloads run fast and stay stable.
